If you compare Japanese cartoons to American cartoons for children, you will (or even might not) be aware of some major differences in the themes and morals portrayed in the content: quite a bit of anime has historical or cultural backing that is rooted deeply in their history (and sometimes even the history of foreign cultures). Through the style of dress, the subject matters, and references to ancient myths they create an entertainment experience that also educates their youth on the history of their nation. They stay connected to their culture through adapting it for a modern generation and successfully instill why their tradition is important. I've also noticed consistent themes of nationalism and a duty to protect one's people from existential threats. They often make it a point to show distinctions in characters, sometimes even unapologetically giving different races of people different traits.

American cartoons (from what I've observed) are inverted in that respect: the characters are often assorted but they are assorted in such a way that the differences don't matter because every character is different. Abstraction can reach absurd proportions to the point where characters are anthropomorphized inanimate objects without a specific gender or the cartoon even makes it a point to genderbend. While there may be an overarching storyline, there is often heavy undertones of nihilism, existential purposelessness, and a general sense of a lack of consequence.

I think that this isn't an accident and the end result are two very different societies with very different sets of values. Just my two cents though.
